title: Response Caching Middleware
description: Configure the ASP.NET Core response caching middleware to cache entire HTTP responses based on headers and cache profiles.

data.text: Response caching stores an entire HTTP response — headers and body — so that the server skips executing the endpoint logic on subsequent requests. Unlike data caching, where you cache a single object, response caching operates at the HTTP layer. It respects standard HTTP cache headers like Cache-Control and Vary, making it interoperable with CDNs and reverse proxies.

ASP.NET Core includes a built-in Response Caching Middleware that stores responses in an IResponseCache implementation. The default stores entries in memory, but you can swap in a Redis-backed implementation for a distributed response cache across multiple server instances.

terms.definition: Middleware that stores and serves cached HTTP responses based on request headers and cache policies.
An HTTP response header that declares whether a response is cacheable, for how long, and by whom.
An HTTP header that tells the cache to store separate responses for different values of a given header (e.g., Accept-Encoding).
A named set of response cache options defined in configuration and applied via the [ResponseCache] attribute.

data.text: Add the middleware in the request pipeline before authorization middleware. Response caching only works for GET or HEAD requests and requires the Cache-Control header to be set by the endpoint or action.

data.title: Registering Response Caching Middleware
data.content: Enable the middleware and add a named cache profile in configuration.

data.title: Applying Response Cache to an Endpoint
data.content: Use the ResponseCache attribute or a cache profile to control caching behavior per endpoint.

data.title: Authorization Prevents Caching
data.text: By default, responses to authorized requests are never cached. The middleware skips caching when an Authorization header is present unless you explicitly set VaryByQueryKeys or use a custom policy.

data.caption: Response caching middleware request processing
data.definition:
flowchart TD
    A[Incoming GET Request] --> B[Check Response Cache]
    B -->|Hit| C[Return Cached Response]
    B -->|Miss| D{Has Authorization Header?}
    D -->|Yes| E[Skip Cache, Execute Endpoint]
    D -->|No| F[Execute Endpoint Logic]
    F --> G{Response Cacheable?}
    G -->|Yes| H[Store Response in Cache]
    G -->|No| I[Return Response, Do Not Cache]
    H --> J[Return Response to Client]
    I --> J
    E --> J
    C --> J

data.text: When your endpoint returns different content based on query parameters, use VaryByQueryKeys to store separate cached responses for each distinct query combination. This is critical for search endpoints, filtered lists, and paginated APIs.

data.title: VaryByQueryKeys Example
data.content: Cache a separate response for each unique search query.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Response caching operates at the HTTP layer, caching full responses
Only GET and HEAD requests are cached by default
Cache profiles centralize settings and can be shared across endpoints
VaryByQueryKeys creates separate cache entries per query combination
Authorized requests are not cached unless explicitly configured
data.takeaway: Response caching is ideal for public, read-heavy GET endpoints with consistent output.
